arxiv-2101-04455.title: Dynamical large deviations for plasmas below the Debye length and the Landau equation Journal: Journal of Statistical Physics
arxiv-2101-04455.creator: Ouassim Feliachi, Freddy Bouchet
arxiv-2101-04455.description: Abstract We consider a homogeneous plasma composed of N N particles of the same electric charge which interact through a Coulomb potential. In the large plasma parameter limit, classical kinetic theories justify that the empirical density is the solution of the Balescu–Guernsey–Lenard equation, at leading order. This is a law of large numbers.

arxiv-2102-09293.title: Convolution of a symmetric log-concave distribution and a symmetric bimodal distribution can have any number of modes
arxiv-2102-09293.creator: Charles Arnal
arxiv-2102-09293.description: Abstract . In this note, we show that the convolution of a discrete symmetric log-concave distribution and a discrete symmetric bimodal distribution can have any strictly positive number of modes. A similar result is proved for smooth distributions, which contradicts the main statement in [ HLL+17 ] . 1.

arxiv-2104-12783.title: Hearing Higgs with Gravitational Wave Detectors
arxiv-2104-12783.creator: Alberto Salvio
arxiv-2104-12783.description: Abstract ——————————————————————————————————————————– Abstract The relic gravitational wave background due to tensor linear perturbations generated during Higgs inflation is computed. Both the Standard Model and a well-motivated phenomenological completion (that accounts for all the experimentally confirmed evidence of new physics) are considered.

arxiv-2108-00472.title: Interference effects in one-dimensional moiré crystals.
arxiv-2108-00472.creator: Nils Wittemeier, Matthieu J. Verstraete, Pablo Ordejón, Zeila Zanolli
arxiv-2108-00472.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Nils Wittemeier, Matthieu J. Verstraete, Pablo Ordejón, Zeila Zanolli. Interference effects in finite sections of one-dimensional moiré crystals are investigated using a Landauer-Büttiker formalism within the tight-binding approximation. We explain interlayer transport in double-wall carbon nanotubes and design a predictive model. Wave function interference is visible at the mesoscale: in the strong coupling regime, as a periodic modulation of quantum conductance and emergent localized states; in the localized-insulating regime, as a suppression of interlayer transport, and oscillations of the density of states.

arxiv-2112-13855.title: Linear growth of structure in projected massive gravity
arxiv-2112-13855.creator: Yusuke Manita, Rampei Kimura
arxiv-2112-13855.description: Abstract In the present paper, we investigate the linear growth of matter fluctuations based on a concrete model of the projected massive gravity, which is free of the Boulware-Deser ghost and preserves the global Lorentz symmetry. We found that at subhorizon scales, the modification to the linear growth is strongly suppressed even without nonlinear screening of an additional force.

arxiv-2404-09034.title: Using Biot-Savart boundary conditions for unbounded external flow on Eulerian meshes
arxiv-2404-09034.creator: Gabriel D. Weymouth, Marin Lauber
arxiv-2404-09034.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Gabriel D. Weymouth, Marin Lauber. We introduce a novel boundary condition for incompressible Eulerian simulations formulated using a Biot-Savart vorticity integral that maintains high-accuracy results even when the domain boundary is within a body-length of immersed solid boundaries. The key prerequisite to accurately couple the Biot-Savart condition to the Eulerian velocity and pressure fields is including the influence of the vorticity generated at the immersed boundaries during the incompressible-flow projection step.

arxiv-2411-18791.title: Miniature UAV-Aided Cooperative THz Networks with Reconfigurable Energy Harvesting Holographic Surfaces
arxiv-2411-18791.creator: Yifei Song, Jalal Jalali, Yanyu Qin, Mostafa Darabi, Filip Lemic, and Natasha Devroye
arxiv-2411-18791.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yifei Song, Jalal Jalali, Yanyu Qin, Mostafa Darabi, Filip Lemic, and Natasha Devroye. This paper focuses on enhancing the energy efficiency (EE) of a cooperative network that features a miniature unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) operating at terahertz (THz) frequencies and equipped with holographic surfaces to improve network performance. Unlike traditional reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), which serve as passive relays for signal reflection, this work introduces a novel concept: energy harvesting (EH) using reconfigurable holographic surfaces (RHS).

arxiv-2502-05208.title: Mitigation of Camouflaged Adversarial Attacks in Autonomous Vehicles–A Case Study Using CARLA Simulator
arxiv-2502-05208.creator: Yago Romano Martinez, Brady Carter, Abhijeet Solanki, Wesam Al Amiri, Syed Rafay Hasan, Terry N. Guo
arxiv-2502-05208.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yago Romano Martinez, Brady Carter, Abhijeet Solanki, Wesam Al Amiri, Syed Rafay Hasan, Terry N. Guo. Autonomous vehicles (AVs) rely heavily on cameras and artificial intelligence (AI) to make safe and accurate driving decisions. However, since AI is the core enabling technology, this raises serious cyber threats that hinder the large-scale adoption of AVs. Therefore, it becomes crucial to analyze the resilience of AV security systems against sophisticated attacks that manipulate camera inputs, deceiving AI models.

arxiv-2509-05548.title: Graphical small cancellation and hyperfiniteness of boundary actions
arxiv-2509-05548.creator: Chris Karpinski, Damian Osajda, Koichi Oyakawa
arxiv-2509-05548.description: Abstract We study actions of (infinitely presented) graphical small cancellation groups on the Gromov boundaries of their coned-off Cayley graphs. We show that a class of graphical small cancellation groups, including (infinitely presented) classical small cancellation groups, admit hyperfinite boundary actions, more precisely, the orbit equivalence relation that they induce on the boundaries of the coned-off Cayley graphs is hyperfinite.

pmc-10509165.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). mRNA vaccines have emerged as highly effective strategies in the prophylaxis and treatment of diseases, thanks largely although not totally to their extraordinary performance in recent years against the worldwide plague COVID-19. pmc-11322059.title: Ventricular-subventricular zone stem cell niche adaptations in a mouse model of post-infectious hydrocephalus

Congenital post-infectious hydrocephalus (PIH) is a condition characterized by enlargement of the ventricular system, consequently imposing a burden on the associated stem cell niche, the ventricular-subventricular zone (V-SVZ). pmc-12662918.title: Evaluating the Ecological Conditions of a Semi-Arid River Basin: A Multimetric Index Incorporating Fish and Macroinvertebrate assemblages
pmc-12662918.creator: Mojgan Zare Shahraki, Ali Reza Esmaeili Ofogh, Pejman Fathi, Joseph Flotemersch, Karen Blocksom, Andreas Bruder
pmc-12662918.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The health and integrity of freshwater ecosystems are significantly affected by anthropogenic pressures. Understanding the ecological conditions of freshwater ecosystems is crucial for effective conservation and management strategies. In this study, we developed a new multimetric index, the Karun Fish-Macroinvertebrate Index (KFMI), that incorporates data on fish and macroinvertebrate assemblages to assess the ecological conditions of the Karun River basin, in Iran. We sampled 53 sites and collected data on fish and macroinvertebrate communities, physicochemical parameters, and habitat characteristics.

pmc-12820378.title: The lived experience of mask wearing among patients with chronic illnesses during the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-12820378.creator: Parvaneh Aghajari, Mina Hosseinzadeh, Zahra Sheikhalipour
pmc-12820378.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The COVID-19 pandemic necessitated widespread mask-wearing as a key preventive measure. While masks played a crucial role in limiting virus transmission, their implications for individuals living with chronic illnesses remain underexplored. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences of patients with chronic conditions regarding mask-wearing during and after the COVID-19 pandemic, with a focus on physical, psychological, and social aspects.

pmc-13121256.title: The muscle dysmorphia–eating disorders link as a public health concern: an epidemiological study of symptom dimensions and social isolation
pmc-13121256.creator: Francesco Leonforte, Michelangelo Mercogliano, Vito Nicosia, Manuela Lo Bianco, Roberta Leonardi, Andrea Cavallaro, Martino Ruggieri, Antonio Mistretta
pmc-13121256.description: BackgroundEating disorders (EDs) represent a growing public health concern among university students, who face critical developmental transitions and increasing pressure from “fitness culture.” This study examined the complex relationship between muscle dysmorphia (MD) symptomatology and ED risk, analyzing how specific psychopathological dimensions interact with socio-demographic variables and lifestyles.

pmc-13393857.title: Toward a model of repeat-driven chromosomal fragility in Triticeae: an integrated structural omics perspective
pmc-13393857.creator: Michał T Kwiatek
pmc-13393857.description: BackgroundRepetitive DNA dominates cereals genomes and plays a major yet poorly understood role in shaping structural genome variation. Recent advances in long-read sequencing, pangenomics, and 3D chromatin mapping have revealed that chromosomal rearrangements in Triticeae frequently arise within repeat-rich heterochromatin. However, the molecular and structural omics determinants underlying this recurrent fragility remain largely unresolved.
